# Turning Chicken Match into a PWA

This guide converts `matchGame` into an installable Progressive Web App while keeping the current Vite and Kaplay setup.

A PWA needs four pieces:

1. A web app manifest.
2. App icons.
3. A service worker for offline caching.
4. HTTPS in production, or `localhost` during development.

The project already uses Vite with `base: "./"`, so relative URLs work when the game is deployed under a subfolder. The game is designed as a 16:9 landscape experience, which is a good fit for iPad and landscape iPhone play.

## Mobile sizing strategy

Keep the internal game world at 320x180. This lets the existing card positions and touch hitboxes stay predictable. Kaplay scales that world into the available device space with letterboxing:

```js
const k = kaplay({
  width: 320,
  height: 180,
  stretch: true,
  letterbox: true,
});
```

`stretch: true` fills the available canvas area. `letterbox: true` preserves the 16:9 ratio instead of stretching the art or hitboxes. On a portrait iPhone, the installed app requests landscape orientation from the manifest; in a browser tab, users should rotate the phone for the intended layout.

## 1. Add the manifest

Create `matchGame/public/manifest.webmanifest`:

```json
{
  "name": "Chicken Match",
  "short_name": "Chicken Match",
  "description": "A three-of-a-kind chicken memory game.",
  "start_url": "./",
  "scope": "./",
  "display": "standalone",
  "orientation": "landscape",
  "background_color": "#18211f",
  "theme_color": "#f4c95d",
  "icons": [
    {
      "src": "./icons/chicken-match-192.png",
      "sizes": "192x192",
      "type": "image/png",
      "purpose": "any maskable"
    },
    {
      "src": "./icons/chicken-match-512.png",
      "sizes": "512x512",
      "type": "image/png",
      "purpose": "any maskable"
    }
  ]
}
```

`start_url` and `scope` use `./` so the game can run at a URL such as `/chickenmatch/` instead of only at the domain root.

## 2. Add app icons

Create `matchGame/public/icons/` and add these PNG files:

```text
matchGame/public/icons/chicken-match-192.png
matchGame/public/icons/chicken-match-512.png
```

Export square PNGs at the exact sizes above. Use the chicken or egg artwork with enough padding that it remains visible when cropped into a maskable icon shape. Do not use the Aseprite source files directly in the manifest.

## 3. Update `index.html`

Use a complete document in `matchGame/index.html` with a mobile viewport and a canvas that fills the safe area:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, viewport-fit=cover" />
    <meta name="theme-color" content="#18211f" />
    <link rel="manifest" href="./manifest.webmanifest" />
    <title>Chicken Match</title>
    <style>
      html, body {
        width: 100%;
        height: 100%;
        margin: 0;
        overflow: hidden;
        overscroll-behavior: none;
        background: #18211f;
      }

      body {
        min-height: 100dvh;
        padding: env(safe-area-inset-top) env(safe-area-inset-right)
          env(safe-area-inset-bottom) env(safe-area-inset-left);
        touch-action: none;
      }

      canvas {
        display: block;
        width: 100%;
        height: 100%;
        touch-action: none;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <script src="src/main.js" type="module"></script>
    <script>
      if ("serviceWorker" in navigator) {
        window.addEventListener("load", () => {
          navigator.serviceWorker.register("./sw.js");
        });
      }
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

The viewport metadata makes the game fit phone screens. The relative manifest URL matches the Vite configuration.

## 4. Add a service worker

Create `matchGame/public/sw.js`:

```js
const CACHE_NAME = "chicken-match-v1";

self.addEventListener("install", (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.open(CACHE_NAME).then((cache) => {
      const base = new URL("./", self.registration.scope).pathname;
      return cache.addAll([
        base,
        `${base}index.html`,
        `${base}manifest.webmanifest`,
        `${base}icons/chicken-match-192.png`,
        `${base}icons/chicken-match-512.png`,
      ]);
    }),
  );
});

self.addEventListener("activate", (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((cacheNames) =>
      Promise.all(
        cacheNames
          .filter((cacheName) => cacheName !== CACHE_NAME)
          .map((cacheName) => caches.delete(cacheName)),
      ),
    ),
  );
});

self.addEventListener("fetch", (event) => {
  if (event.request.method !== "GET") return;

  event.respondWith(
    caches.match(event.request).then((cachedResponse) => {
      if (cachedResponse) return cachedResponse;

      return fetch(event.request).then((networkResponse) => {
        const responseCopy = networkResponse.clone();
        caches.open(CACHE_NAME).then((cache) => {
          cache.put(event.request, responseCopy);
        });
        return networkResponse;
      });
    }),
  );
});
```

This caches the app shell and then caches successful GET requests such as the Kaplay bundle, images, and sounds as they load. Change the cache strategy later if large media files need more careful update behavior.

## 5. Register the service worker

Add this after the existing module script in `matchGame/index.html`:

```html
<script src="src/main.js" type="module"></script>
<script>
  if ("serviceWorker" in navigator) {
    window.addEventListener("load", () => {
      navigator.serviceWorker.register("./sw.js");
    });
  }
</script>
```

Because `sw.js` is in `public/`, Vite emits it beside the built `index.html`, allowing it to control the game and its descendants.

## 6. Check asset paths

Vite copies `matchGame/public/` directly into the build output:

```text
public/sprites/chicken.png -> dist/sprites/chicken.png
public/sounds/chicken-select.mp3 -> dist/sounds/chicken-select.mp3
public/manifest.webmanifest -> dist/manifest.webmanifest
public/sw.js -> dist/sw.js
```

Use relative game asset paths so deployment under a subfolder works:

```js
k.loadSprite("chicken", "sprites/chicken.png");
k.loadSound("burk", "sounds/chicken-select.mp3");
```

Avoid leading `/` paths for assets. A leading slash points to the domain root and can fail when the game is hosted at `/chickenmatch/`:

```js
k.loadSound("burk", "sounds/chicken-select.mp3");
```

## 7. Build and test locally

From `matchGame/`:

```sh
npm run build
npm run preview
```

Open the preview URL printed by Vite. Service workers require HTTPS, but browsers treat `localhost` as a secure development origin.

Check the following in Chromium DevTools:

1. Application > Manifest: the manifest loads and icons are valid.
2. Application > Service Workers: `sw.js` is running.
3. Application > Cache Storage: the app shell is cached.
4. Lighthouse: installability and offline checks pass.

To test offline mode, load the game once, enable the browser's Offline network setting, and reload. Confirm that the shell and already-cached assets still load.

## 8. Test iPhone and iPad layouts

Use Safari Web Inspector or Chrome DevTools device emulation first, then test on real hardware:

1. Test an iPhone in portrait and landscape. Landscape is the intended play orientation.
2. Test an iPad in both orientations and at split-screen widths.
3. Confirm the canvas remains centered, the 3x3 card grid is fully visible, and no page scrolling occurs.
4. Tap every card and the reset button; do not rely only on mouse clicks.
5. Test with the browser UI visible and as an installed standalone PWA, because their safe-area sizes differ.
6. Load the game once, turn on Offline mode, and reload to verify cached assets.

If the game feels too small on a portrait phone, do not stretch it independently on the x and y axes. Keep the letterbox behavior and guide the player to rotate the device; independent stretching makes the pixel art and touch coordinates inconsistent.

## 9. Deploy over HTTPS

Production service workers require HTTPS. Deploy to a host such as GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, or another HTTPS server.

Verify these URLs from the final deployment path:

```text
https://example.com/game/manifest.webmanifest
https://example.com/game/sw.js
https://example.com/game/
```

The current relative Vite base supports a repository subpath, but test the published URL rather than only the local preview.

## 10. Update the cache on releases

For each release:

1. Change `CACHE_NAME` from `chicken-match-v1` to `chicken-match-v2`.
2. Run `npm run build`.
3. Deploy the new `dist/` contents.
4. Reload once so the new worker installs and removes the old cache.

Changing the cache name prevents users from being stuck with old JavaScript, images, or sounds.

## PWA checklist

- [ ] `manifest.webmanifest` returns HTTP 200.
- [ ] Valid 192px and 512px PNG icons exist.
- [ ] `sw.js` returns HTTP 200.
- [ ] The service worker is registered under the game URL.
- [ ] Asset paths work under a deployment subfolder.
- [ ] The game reloads with the network disabled.
- [ ] Production uses HTTPS.
- [ ] The cache version changes with each release.
- [ ] Standalone mode is tested on a real phone or tablet.
